chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked him about the skin of a dead animal: may it be worn in salat (prayer) if it has been tanned? He said: “No, even if it is tanned seventy times.”

key_terms.الْجِلْدِ: skin or hide used as clothing material
key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: that which comes from a dead animal not lawfully slaughtered
key_terms.دُبِغَ: was tanned or processed as leather
key_terms.سَبْعِينَ: seventy, used here for emphatic intensification

ai.seo_question: Can tanned skin from a dead animal be worn during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning salat (prayer) and clothing made from the skin of a dead animal. It states that tanning does not make such skin permissible to wear in salat (prayer), emphasizing the ruling with strong wording.
